- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak value by 5–10% and smooth transition to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model often overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast growth to 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., >10% gap), apply upward bias correction proportional to sentiment volatility (higher sentiment → higher correction).
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows recent divergence (e.g., high sentiment but low price), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, especially if price is below 10-day moving average.
